title: θ ∼ x ⟺ π ∼ x/log x: The Chebyshev–Prime-Counting Form of PNT
description: Closes the first open question of chebyshev-bounds-oq-03: the equivalence θ(x) ∼ x ⟺ π(x) ∼ x/log x between the prime-log sum θ and the prime-counting function π. Rather than Abel summation it uses the elementary two-inequality argument (Apostol, Thm 4.4): θ(x) ≤ π(x)·log x (every prime p ≤ x contributes log p ≤ log x) and π(x) ≤ x^α + θ(x)/(α·log x) for 0 < α < 1 (split the primes at x^α; those above contribute log p > α·log x). Dividing by x sandwiches the two ratios within a factor 1/α; since x^{α−1}·log x → 0 and α may approach 1, θ(x)/x → 1 ⟺ π(x)·log x/x → 1. Combined with the parent's ψ ∼ θ, all three classical forms of PNT are equivalent, from Chebyshev-level tools only. All 0 axioms.

relatedProblems.relationship: Parent: proved ψ ∼ θ and asked (OQ-03's first open question) to complete the chain θ ∼ x ⟺ π ∼ x/log x. This entry answers exactly that.

overview.historicalContext: The Prime Number Theorem can be stated in three classical, equivalent forms: ψ(x) ∼ x, θ(x) ∼ x, and π(x) ∼ x/log x, where θ(x) = Σ_{p≤x} log p, ψ(x) = Σ_{p^k≤x} log p, and π(x) = #{p ≤ x}. The standard route proves one form and transfers across the equivalences. The parent gallery chain established ψ ∼ θ (prime powers are negligible). The remaining link, θ ∼ x ⟺ π ∼ x/log x, connects a sum weighted by log p to a plain count. It is usually presented via Abel (partial) summation, but it also has a fully elementary proof (Apostol, Introduction to Analytic Number Theory, Theorem 4.4) requiring only two inequalities — which is what this entry formalizes.
overview.problemStatement: Prove the equivalence θ(x) ∼ x ⟺ π(x) ∼ x/log x, formalized as Tendsto (θ x / x) atTop (𝓝 1) ↔ Tendsto (π(x)·log x / x) atTop (𝓝 1), thereby completing the PNT equivalence chain ψ ∼ x ⟺ θ ∼ x ⟺ π ∼ x/log x entirely from Chebyshev-level tools (no contour integration, no zeta function).
overview.proofStrategy: Two bracketing inequalities. (A) θ(x) = Σ_{p≤x} log p ≤ Σ_{p≤x} log x = π(x)·log x, since each prime p ≤ x has log p ≤ log x. (B) For 0 < α < 1, split the primes ≤ x at x^α: those ≤ x^α number at most x^α, while each prime p with x^α < p ≤ x satisfies log p > log(x^α) = α·log x, so the count of those is ≤ (θ(x)−θ(x^α))/(α·log x) ≤ θ(x)/(α·log x); hence π(x) ≤ x^α + θ(x)/(α·log x). Writing f(x) = θ(x)/x and g(x) = π(x)·log x/x and dividing through, (A) gives f ≤ g and (B) gives g ≤ x^{α−1}·log x + (1/α)·f. The error term x^{α−1}·log x → 0 (log = o(x^{1−α})), so the two ratios are trapped within a factor 1/α of each other; letting α → 1 via the order-topology characterization tendsto_order forces them to share the limit 1. Each direction of the ⟺ chooses α as a function of the target neighborhood (α = 2/(1+b) for the upper bound, α = (max 0 b + 1)/2 for the lower).
keyInsights: θ and π are two ways of weighing the primes up to x — by log p, or by 1 — and the transfer needs only that log p lies between α·log x and log x for the bulk of primes.
The easy inequality θ ≤ π·log x is immediate; the content is the reverse, where splitting at x^α discards a negligible head (≤ x^α primes) and bounds the tail by θ(x)/(α·log x).
Dividing by x sandwiches θ(x)/x and π(x)·log x/x within the factor 1/α; the single analytic input is the decay x^{α−1}·log x → 0, i.e. log grows slower than any positive power.
The α → 1 limit is the crux, and the order-topology characterization tendsto_order turns it into a clean choice of α per target neighborhood — no limsup/liminf bookkeeping.
Combined with the parent's ψ ∼ θ, this closes the loop: all three forms ψ ∼ x, θ ∼ x, π ∼ x/log x are equivalent using only Chebyshev-level estimates.

sections.title: Header: The θ–π Form of the Prime Number Theorem
sections.summary: States the parent's open question — complete the equivalence chain by proving θ(x) ∼ x ⟺ π(x) ∼ x/log x via partial summation between the prime-log sum and the prime-counting function. This file closes the gap with Apostol's elementary two-inequality argument instead of Abel summation: θ(x) ≤ π(x)·log x (each prime p ≤ x contributes log p ≤ log x) and π(x) ≤ x^α + θ(x)/(α log x) for 0 < α < 1 (split primes at x^α); dividing by x and letting α → 1 forces θ(x)/x and π(x)·log x/x to share a limit, so θ(x) ∼ x iff π(x) ∼ x/log x, completing the equivalence of all three classical PNT forms from Chebyshev-level tools alone.
sections.mathContext: $\theta(x) \le \pi(x)\log x \le x^{\alpha}\log x + \tfrac{1}{\alpha}\theta(x)$ for $0<\alpha<1$; letting $\alpha \to 1$ gives $\theta(x)/x \to 1 \iff \pi(x)\log x/x \to 1$.

sections.title: Section I: θ's Index Set Is the Prime-Counting Function
sections.summary: primeCountingReal packages π(⌊x⌋) as a real number; theta_eq_sum unfolds θ; card_filter_prime_Ioc proves #((Ioc 0 n).filter Prime) = π(n), identifying the support of θ with the primes counted by π.
sections.mathContext: θ sums log p over exactly the primes that π counts — the bridge that lets the two functions be compared.

sections.title: Section II: The Easy Inequality θ(x) ≤ π(x)·log x
sections.summary: theta_le_primeCounting_mul_log: bounding each term log p ≤ log x and summing gives θ(x) ≤ π(x)·log x for x ≥ 1.
sections.mathContext: Every prime ≤ x contributes at most log x, so the log-weighted sum is at most the count times log x.

sections.title: Section III: The Hard Inequality π(x) ≤ x^α + θ(x)/(α·log x)
sections.summary: primeCounting_le: split the primes ≤ x at x^α. The head (primes ≤ x^α) numbers at most x^α; each prime in the tail (x^α < p ≤ x) has log p > α·log x, so the tail numbers at most θ(x)/(α·log x).
sections.mathContext: Discarding a negligible head of ≤ x^α primes, the remaining primes are bounded by the log-weighted sum divided by the threshold α·log x.

sections.title: Section IV: θ ∼ x ⟺ π ∼ x/log x
sections.summary: theta_asymp_iff_primeCounting_asymp: from f ≤ g ≤ x^{α−1}·log x + (1/α)·f and x^{α−1}·log x → 0, the order-topology characterization with α → 1 gives θ(x)/x → 1 ⟺ π(x)·log x/x → 1.
sections.mathContext: The two normalized counting functions share the limit 1: the PNT in θ-form holds iff it holds in π-form.

conclusion.summary: A fully verified (0 sorries, 0 axioms, no native_decide) file of 250 lines establishing the θ–π form of the Prime Number Theorem: θ(x) ∼ x ⟺ π(x) ∼ x/log x. The heart is two bracketing inequalities — θ(x) ≤ π(x)·log x and π(x) ≤ x^α + θ(x)/(α·log x) — which sandwich the normalized functions within a factor 1/α; the decay x^{α−1}·log x → 0 and the limit α → 1 (via tendsto_order) collapse the sandwich to a shared limit.
conclusion.implications: This answers the first open question of the parent chebyshev-bounds-oq-03, completing the PNT equivalence chain ψ ∼ x ⟺ θ ∼ x ⟺ π ∼ x/log x entirely with Chebyshev-level tools. The elementary two-inequality route (Apostol Thm 4.4) is formalized in place of Abel summation, and the bracketing lemmas — θ ≤ π·log x and π ≤ x^α + θ/(α·log x) — are reusable for converting between log-weighted prime sums and prime counts in other analytic-number-theory formalizations.
openQuestions: Combine with the parent's ψ ∼ θ to package all three PNT forms (ψ ∼ x, θ ∼ x, π ∼ x/log x) as a single equivalence theorem, so a proof of any one transfers to the others.
Quantify the transfer: from explicit Chebyshev bounds c₁x ≤ θ(x) ≤ c₂x, deduce explicit bounds on π(x)·log x/x, recovering a Chebyshev-type two-sided estimate for π.
